title: PG-03.5 Cross-language protocol vectors (crdt-merge-rs)
request: Programme contract for work package WP03 in crdt-merge-rs: Cross-language protocol vectors. Supersedes PG-03.3 (signed; the PG-03.3 file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this contract). Reason: the signed PG-03.3 cannot be met as scoped because the Rust edition lacks the features its vectors need (an ORSet type key, optional tombstones on read, the canonical sort, LWWMap, AgentState, and node_id on LWWRegister); the signer decided to supersede it with a contract that builds them. Depends on contracts: PG-03.1 (signed). The Python serialisation is that of crdt-merge main 252c93e6; the canonical form and vectors are those of crdt-merge pull request #183 (commit b92d0ef). Implemented by the draft pull request #1 of the edition repository; no head sha is pinned. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. Source: the programme decomposition of 31 Oct 2026 (docs/scope-one/programme/WBS.md, docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md, docs/scope-one/programme/fragments/WP03.json) and the owner notes behind docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md. Depends on tasks outside this contract: WP03-01. Covers only what the Scope One contracts (SO-1.01 to SO-1.11) do not already cover; the mapping is in contracts/programme/manifest.json.   Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.title: ORSet, LWWMap, LWWRegister and the canonical form in the Rust edition
requirements: MV-DEM-06: Python, Rust and TypeScript nodes exchange identical protocol representations (P2). (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:74; evidence docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md:111; baseline 8.5)

The Python serialisation to match is that of crdt-merge main 252c93e6 (ORSet tombstones from pull request #180, merged through pull request #181); the canonical form and the vectors are those of crdt-merge pull request #183, pinned at commit b92d0ef in tests/vectors/SOURCE (source: crdt-merge main 252c93e6; crdt-merge pull request #183; contract PG-03.1, cited by id)

Vector numbers are never whole-number floats and never use exponent notation: TypeScript prints 5 where Python and Rust print 5.0, and cross-language float printing is out of scope (normative, owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

LWWRegister merge: a higher timestamp wins; on equal timestamps the greater node_id wins. Equal timestamp and equal node_id is a known open gap: the Python reference keeps self and Rust keeps other, so merge is not commutative there. That case is excluded from the vectors and must not be asserted; it is recorded in docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md as an open follow-up against the crdt-merge reference, which is fixed first and the editions follow (normative, owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

An unknown element_types name is read as a string, matching the reference. A typed Rust ORSet<String> may reject typed elements on read; that is allowed and must be documented (normative, owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

Canonical order: object keys and set members sort by Unicode code point. The TypeScript UTF-16 comparison differs only for astral characters, which the vectors exclude; that is a known limitation and is noted in the edition (normative, owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)
tasks.description: Repo: crdt-merge-rs. ORSet in src/core.rs gets the type key and optional sorted tombstones and element_types; remove() writes tombstones and an emptied element keeps its key, and a stale replica does not resurrect a removed element. LWWRegister carries {value, timestamp, node_id} with a Timestamp, and the greater node id settles a tie. LWWMap, Element and WireElement are added in src/core.rs. src/canonical.rs holds the canonical form of crdt-merge pull request #183. A typed ORSet<String> may reject typed elements on read and ORSet<Element> reads every type; this is allowed and is documented.

criteria.statement: The wire-form tests (ORSet, LWWRegister, LWWMap, canonical form) fail before and pass after
The tests cover tombstones, resurrection, node_id, the canonical form and the typed-element rule

verifier.cmd: for n in "tombstone" "resurrect" "node_id" "canonicalize" "rejects_a_typed_element"; do grep -qi "$n" tests/wire_tests.rs || exit 1; done

criteria.statement: src/core.rs defines WireElement, Timestamp and LWWMap

verifier.cmd: grep -q WireElement src/core.rs && grep -q Timestamp src/core.rs && grep -q LWWMap src/core.rs

criteria.statement: src/canonical.rs exists and src/lib.rs exports it
The edition builds

tasks.description: Repo: crdt-merge-rs. tests/vectors/ is copied unchanged from crdt-merge at the commit pinned in tests/vectors/SOURCE (b92d0ef, pull request #183): SOURCE, orset.json, lwwmap.json and agentstate.json. No vector is edited, excluded or ignored to pass. The 33 vectors (20 states and 13 merges) are re-emitted byte-identically, merged in both orders and checked against the recorded value; before the change the vector tests failed, among them the 19 ORSet vectors. The implementing pull request measured these counts; they are a floor for information and no exact count is a criterion. Measured: 129 tests in the full suite. CI runs cargo test. Known limitations are listed in CHANGELOG.md: whole-number float printing, the equal node id tie, unknown element types and the typed ORSet<String> read. Keys sort by code point, which is byte order for UTF-8.

criteria.statement: Every vector in tests/vectors/** is read and re-emitted byte-identically
cargo test passes
tests/vectors/SOURCE pins crdt-merge commit b92d0ef (pull request #183)
The ORSet vector file exists
The LWWMap vector file exists
The AgentState vector file exists
The vector test reads the three vector files
The vector test ignores and excludes no vector
No vector holds a whole-number float or exponent notation (rule: Python and Rust print 5.0, TypeScript prints 5)

verifier.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");let bad=0;for(const f of fs.readdirSync("tests/vectors")){if(!f.endsWith(".json"))continue;const t=fs.readFileSync("tests/vectors/"+f,"utf8").replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/g,"\"\"");if(/\d\.0+(?![0-9])|\d[eE][+-]?\d/.test(t)){console.log("bad number in "+f);bad=1}}process.exit(bad)'

CHANGELOG.md lists the known limitations: whole-number floats, the equal node id tie, unknown element types and the typed ORSet<String> read that rejects typed elements
